newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipinos slam death of students in crossfire.
newsitem.headline: Filipinos slam death of students in crossfire.

text.p: Thousands of Moslem residents rallied on Sunday to denounce the death of 10 Filipino Moslem students and their teacher who were killed in crossfire between government and Moslem rebels in southern Philippines.

"We are urging all Moslems to bind ourselves until justice be given to the 11 Moslem victims," Hajih Abdullah Laxaman, organiser of the rally, told the crowd which was made up mostly of Moslem women wearing black veils.
He accused the Philippine Army of misfiring their mortars into a school instead of a military camp of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front in Buldon town in Maguindanao on March 15.
Police chief Major Sanny Dampac estimated the crowd which massed at the public square of Marawi city, 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila, at between 10,000 and 13,000.
In Manila, defense secretary Renato de Villa told reporters that a joint investigation panel would be organised to probe the incident which army officials had denied they initiated.
"We got in touch right away with the leadership of the MILF, and they have agreed to meet with us as soon as possible," de Villa said.
Military officials confirmed there had been a gunbattle in the area but said no army mortar had hit the school.
The incident occurred while a ceasefire was in effect to facilitate the peace talks between the government and the MILF which has been fighting for an Islamic state in the southern Philippine island.
